name: ai_step
description: Do ONE act in the game as the character, wait until the game has settled, and read what changed. Answers one line of JSON: ok, mode, did, why_not, hint, now. `now` holds only what changed since your last call: where, fight, countdown, can, party, waiting, near, heard, events, notes (and in mode open: rolls, scenes, route). If `now.waiting` is not empty, answer it first, exactly as its line says. When ok is false nothing was done: read why_not and make the call that hint gives.

do.description: The act. go: walk to target. use: walk up and use target (door, lever, ladder, pod). talk: walk up and talk to target. loot: walk up and open target (a body, a chest). jump: jump to target. examine: read a creature in the game's Examine window (type, level, HP, AC, abilities, conditions, resistances, notable features, saves). cast: use the action `spell` at target. attack: weapon attack at target. end: end the turn. select: take control of party member `who`. answer: choose answer number `n` of what waits. continue: go on in a dialogue; press a key on the splash screen. roll: throw the dice of a roll window. take: take everything from the open loot window. close: close the window that waits; skip a film. ui: use a window's controls - with `window` only, list them; with `control`, click it; with `control` and `value`, set it. wait: do nothing until the game has settled. plan: do the act that now.route names (mode open). cheat_cast: cast `spell` at target by script. cheat_teleport: put the character at target. The two cheats are used only when the owner says so.

window.description: For ui: the name of an open window, as now.waiting names it (like MainMenu or CharacterCreation).

control.description: For ui: a control's handle, as the list of the window's controls (now.window) gives it.

value.description: For ui: the value to set (a list's item by number or text, a slider's number, a text); without control, a part of a handle or text that finds controls.

target.description: What the act is done to: a handle from now.near (like #1a2b3c), a name, or a point as text "x,y,z".

spell.description: For cast: the action's name as now.can lists it (like Projectile_FireBolt).

n.description: For answer: the number of the answer, as now.waiting numbers them.

provoke.description: For go in a fight: true walks out of an enemy's reach anyway, taking its opportunity attack (left out, such a walk is refused with who would attack).

who.description: The party member who acts, by name. Left out: in a fight the member whose turn is open, else the character you control.

say.description: A short first-person line shown over the character's head once the act has begun (60 characters at most); not shown when the act is refused.

think.description: Give it on every step: why you do this act, in a few words. Kept in the run's record only, never shown in the game.

goals.description: Your plan, up to 3 short goals separated by | ("kill the archers on the ledge | keep Gale behind the wall | ✓ free Shadowheart"); start a goal with ✓ when it is done; "" forgets them. Kept and told back in now.goals when they change and when a turn opens; shown over the head. Give it with any step, only when the plan changes.

about.description: With note: the creature or thing the note is of (a handle like #1a2b3c, or a name), instead of the place. Its lines then say how many notes it has and the last ("[2 notes: \"betrayed me\"]"); ai_look part=notes about=<it> reads them all. Kept across loads.

note.description: A note to yourself kept with this place, across reloads: you are shown it again when you come back here.

name: ai_look
description: Read the whole situation again, or one part of it, when you are lost. Changes nothing in the game. Answers one line of JSON: ok, mode, did, why_not, hint, now.

part.description: all (default): every key of now as it is at this moment. A key of now: only it, whole (ways also with the open ground you see). things: every object around, items included. actions: what the acting character can do. thoughts: the last reasons (think) given with steps. notes: your notes of this level, or with about every note of one creature or thing. prompt: the owner's text for you, again. rolls, scenes, route, plan (every step of the route): mode open only.

about.description: With part notes: the creature or thing whose notes to read (a handle or a name).

detail.description: brief (default; full for one part): short lists. full: long lists and whole texts.

name: ai_scene
description: The owner's director commands: run a named call of a staged scene, or read a scene's state. Use it only when the owner says so. Answers one line of JSON: ok, mode, did, why_not, hint, now.

name.description: The scene's name as now.scenes shows it. Left out: every scene with its state and calls.

call.description: The call of that scene to run (like go or reply); arm and off arm and disarm a scene of the stand's manifest. Left out: the scene's state and its calls.

file.description: For arm and off: the scene's file, read on the machine that runs the game; given once, the code is kept in the copy and armed again after a reload.

name: ai_session
description: Call this first. It starts the session and answers the owner's own text for you as `prompt` (who you are, what is wanted, how to talk) and the whole situation as `now`. With no arguments it reads the session again and changes nothing. Answers one line of JSON: ok, mode, did, why_not, hint, prompt, now.

mode.description: blind: you are told only what a player at the screen could know. open: everything the bridge can read, with scenes and a route. Left out: the mode stays as it is.

prompt.description: The owner's own text for the model, given as text.

prompt_file.description: The same, given as the path of a plain text file on the machine that runs the game.

scenes_file.description: The path of the stand's manifest of staged scenes (JSON) on the machine that runs the game: what ai_scene arms by name.

plan.description: Mode open only: the name of a route plan to follow (like prologue), or off.

step.description: Mode open only: the number of the plan's step to stand on.

lua: args.prompt_from = args.prompt_file; args.scenes_from = args.scenes_file; return Mods.GateKitAI.AI.Tool('session', args)
